title: Driving and suppressing the human language network using large language models
goal: Recreate the original language-network drive/suppress response effects and linguistic-feature findings, together with the source encoding refit, and assess proposed improvements only against explicitly named, source-matched results.
primary_outputs: Reproduction: executable analysis and source-native outputs for the corrected primary empirical findings: Retain the original five-person/1,000-baseline-item encoding design, three-person/1,500-item event-related search response analysis, its distinct blocked robustness companion, and the source-defined linguistic-feature relationships and controls with their own participant/item support. Preserve original normalization, raw-effect definitions, model controls and participant dependence. Do not infer every figure, all 14 people, all 29 sessions, raw acquisition or new stimulus intervention from the broader report inventory.
Primary improvement: unavailable until a source-grounded same-result comparison is independently justified; no new score or direction is implied.

Retained secondary work: Retain Figure 3 sentence-response prediction as a separately named empirical comparison related to the encoding component; baseline-only and condition-specific results retain their source roles. A higher pooled correlation alone does not establish the whole original finding family or improved biological stimulus control. Preserve the broader source-report inventory as evidence rather than mandatory primary scope. Keep the model-conditioned noise simulation distinct from empirical prediction.
success_criteria: Recreate the corrected primary empirical findings with their source-defined populations, complete required panels and controls.
Use an explicitly bound reproduction proposal only within its declared eligibility, comparison and execution limits; copying published findings is insufficient.

The preserved improvement.v1.json retains its declared comparison and coverage. Use retained_secondary_scope for its relationship to the corrected primary findings; satisfying a secondary or partial-component criterion alone does not establish complete primary reproduction or improvement.

The primary same-target outcome bundle is unavailable. Any primary improvement requires an independently justified source-grounded comparison; no replacement metric, direction or tolerance is invented.
Keep the paper+data and paper+data+author-code outcomes separate. All scientific outcomes remain unknown until qualifying original-data execution and independent verification.
Preserve prior task definitions, improvement criteria and useful secondary implementations with their original scopes. Historical attempts and source metadata do not become qualified AI results.

retained_secondary_improvement.improvement_loop: Once the final source baseline is recovered, develop encoding changes on original train-participant data with training-only validation and a declared feature/model exposure policy. Treat published targets and cached predictions as known exposures that require isolation.
retained_secondary_improvement.candidate_freeze: Seal feature model, preprocessing, fitting/selection recipe and prediction code before original evaluation responses are supplied to the trusted evaluator.
retained_secondary_improvement.final_evaluation: One fixed-protocol comparison on the full original main search set; show source-paper, replayed author and candidate scores separately. No current executable success condition is claimed. Include the original drive/suppress response effects and linguistic-feature controls as calibration/safeguards; no whole-registration victory follows from Fig. 3 alone.
retained_secondary_improvement.baseline_policy: Use the pinned author fit/apply/figure route and preserve its original train/evaluation identities. A locally rewritten ridge baseline, historical numeric-tolerance grader or exploratory modify comparison is not the paper baseline.
